Blackstone stake buy to boost IIFL Finance's capital needs: Fitch Ratings
items.summary:
Blackstone's plan to acquire a 16 per cent stake in IIFL Finance will support the Indian firm's growth capital with an unlikely shift in IIFL's business model, which focuses on secured loans, Fitch Ratings said on Thursday.
Fitch said with the investment, Blackstone would effectively become IIFL Finance's main private-equity shareholder.
Fitch believes that the refreshed shareholder and board composition could alter IIFL's business strategy, risk appetite and growth trajectory.
However, the significant injection of capital and foreign investment supports Indian financial institutions' capital and funding flexibility.
Earlier this month, the board of IIFL Finance approved a plan to raise Rs 6,414 crore through a preferential issue. This included Rs 5,000 crore investment from Blackstone and Rs 1,264 crore by the company's promoters Nirmal Jain and R Venkataraman, besides Rs 150 crore from Anchorage Capital.

items.summary:
Blackstone's plan to acquire a 16 per cent stake in IIFL Finance will support the Indian firm's growth capital with an unlikely shift in IIFL's business model, which focuses on secured loans, Fitch Ratings said on Thursday.
Fitch said with the investment, Blackstone would effectively become IIFL Finance's main private-equity shareholder.
Fitch believes that the refreshed shareholder and board composition could alter IIFL's business strategy, risk appetite and growth trajectory.
However, the significant injection of capital and foreign investment supports Indian financial institutions' capital and funding flexibility.
Earlier this month, the board of IIFL Finance approved a plan to raise Rs 6,414 crore through a preferential issue. This included Rs 5,000 crore investment from Blackstone and Rs 1,264 crore by the company's promoters Nirmal Jain and R Venkataraman, besides Rs 150 crore from Anchorage Capital.

PVR Inox shares jump 6% in 2 days, hit fresh 52-week high as CRISIL upgrades outlook to positive. What is it seeing
items.summary: Shares of PVR Inox jumped around 4% on Wednesday, extending gains to over 6% in two days after ratings agency CRISIL revised its outlook for the firm’s long-term bank facilities and non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to ‘Positive’ from ‘Stable’.PVR Inox shares hit a fresh 52-week high of around Rs 1,740 apiece on NSE today, pushing its market capitalisation above Rs 17,060 crore. Along with the outlook upgrade, CRISIL Ratings also reaffirmed its 'Crisil AA' rating on the long term debt instruments of the company.Why did Crisil upgrade its outlook for PVR Inox?The rating on the short-term bank facilities and commercial paper programme has been reaffirmed at 'Crisil A1+'. The ratings agency said the outlook upgrade was driven by expectations of sustained growth in the company’s scale of operations across multiple revenue streams and improvement in operating margin strengthening its business risk profile. The outlook revision also accounts for the strengthening of the company’s financial risk profile by becoming a net cash company during the first half of fiscal 2027.Also read | District's PVR INOX ticket sales jump 60%, rivals lag at 4%The structural improvement is driven by PVR Inox’s ability to monetise its network more consistently across content cycles, thereby reducing content concentration risk, Crisil said. It added that the content ecosystem has become increasingly diversified, with admissions being supported by a broader mix of Hindi, regional and Hollywood content. The industry has also witnessed increasing success of mid-budget films which lowers the dependence on a few marquee releases and provides greater stability to admissions and occupancy.Alternate content initiatives such as re-releases, concert screenings, anime content and sports broadcasts have also emerged as supplementary demand drivers and improve utilisation of the existing screen network, Crisil said. It noted that the concerns around OTT-led disruption have also moderated as the theatrical-first release model has been re-established, with producers increasingly using theatrical performance as the primary benchmark for content monetisation on OTT, highlighting the complementary nature of theatrical and digital channels.PVR Inox’s business risk profile is also supported by increasing geographical diversification as the company continues to expand its presence in southern India and tier 2 and 3 markets, which benefit from strong movie-going culture, multiple thriving film industries and relatively low multiplex penetration, the ratings agency said, further noting that the company’s screen portfolio in southern markets increased from 31% at the end of fiscal 2023 to 34% in at the end of first half of fiscal 2027, with more than 35% of screen additions over the past three years originating from the region. “This diversification supports admissions visibility and reduces dependence on any single language or regional content cycle,” it said.Crisil further highlighted PVR Inox’s earnings, pointing out that the company demonstrated healthy revenue growth driven by a mix of increasing admissions, increasing average ticket prices (ATP), higher spends per head (SPH), and improving monetisation of its customer base. Net debt reduced, aided by strong accrual generation and proceeds from the divestment of the 4700 BC business for about Rs 227 crore in January 2026. Despite completion of a Rs 300 crore maiden share buyback in the first half of fiscal 2027, leverage metrics are expected to remain comfortable, the ratings agency said. It expects the company’s net worth to remain healthy and gradually improve over the medium term, supported by strong accrual.“The ratings reflect the company’s strong market position with an established brand, expectation of further improvement in operating efficiency, led by synergistic benefits and premiumisation, and a strong financial risk profile. These strengths are partially offset by inherent volatility of the film exhibition business with operating performance remaining dependent on the quality and timing of content releases and evolving consumer preferences,” it said.Also read | PVR INOX bets on smaller multiplexes as single-screens declinePVR Inox share pricePVR Inox shares jumped more than 9% in a week and 23% in a month. This comes amid blockbuster releases including Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Part 1. The stock has so far gained more than 70% in 2026.The shares of the multiplex chain operator have delivered 55% returns over one year. In the longer term, the stock gained more than 4.5% in three years and 2% in five years. The company has a market capitalisation of more than Rs 16,896 crore.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: Anil Agarwal warns Vedanta block transfer to ONGC could deter investors
items.summary:
Mining czar Anil Agarwal on Tuesday warned that the government's decision to transfer operations of a producing offshore oil and gas block from his company to state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) could send wrong signal to investors.
In a LinkedIn post, he urged policymakers to maintain regulatory stability and avoid disrupting existing operators.
"Recently, our running field has been given to ONGC which will send a very wrong signal to investors," he said, referring to the disputed Cambay offshore block in Gujarat that ONGC took over from Vedanta in July following a Delhi High Court ruling.
Agarwal said Vedanta Oil and Gas, which he described as India's largest private-sector producer, was committing USD 5 billion to scale up production to between 300,000 and 500,000 barrels per day. He did not indicate a timeline for reaching the production.
